crossStoryFindings: The archive route and read surfaces exist, but the main process work surface never exposes a user-facing entry point into them, so the end-to-end archive flow stops at the surface boundary instead of starting from `/projects/{projectId}/processes/{processId}` as specified.

Archive append/patch invalidation is wired through the store, but turn/view rebuild paths can still repopulate stale caches during concurrent archive patches because cache rebuild safety is checked against an incomplete archive fingerprint and is skipped entirely on cold-cache GETs.
Both verification gates passed, which means current automated coverage is strong on storage/read/render happy paths but misses archive-surface discoverability and stale-cache race conditions.
architectureFindings: Tech design called for `process-work-surface.ts` to gain archive entry points/actions, but the shared contract still exposes only the pre-Epic-7 control set and the work-surface page only handles those existing actions.

Derived-view conflict handling fingerprints only `archiveEntryId`, `sequence`, and `recordedAt`, even though `patchArchiveEntry` mutates relation and degradation fields that directly affect turn derivation and derived-view status.
epicCoverageAssessment: `corepack pnpm run verify-all` passed locally, including integration tests and `tests/e2e/archive-runtime-flow.spec.ts`.

Coverage is good for archive persistence, read APIs, turn derivation, derived views, and provenance enrichment, but there is no client/integration coverage proving that a user can actually reach the archive surfaces from the process work surface.

The shipped default execution path still does not emit low-level `archiveEntries`, so full taxonomy coverage is mostly proven through storage/service seams and injected fixtures rather than the default runtime flow.
productionPathFindings: No material test fake/stub is wired into the production boot path: `createApp` rejects `NullPlatformStore` in production and defaults to real Local/Daytona adapters plus the real Octokit checkpoint writer.

The default shipped execution payload is still a high-level runtime brief that returns `archiveEntries: []` and one finalized `process_event`, so real low-level archive population depends on injected process-specific execution rather than the default runtime.

Derived-view warm/refresh uses the real persistence path, but concurrent archive patches can still leave stale cached turns/views because the conflict signature ignores mutable archive fields and cold-cache GET rebuilds do not guard for conflicts at all.

blockingFindings.title: Process work surface exposes no archive entry point
blockingFindings.evidence: Epic 7 requires `/projects/{projectId}/processes/{processId}` to provide entry points into archive, turn, and derived-view reads (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/07--archive-and-derived-views/epic.md:469`), and the tech design explicitly says `process-work-surface.ts` should be modified for archive entry points/actions (`.../tech-design.md:162-165`). The current shared contract still only defines `start/respond/resume/rehydrate/rebuild/review/restart` actions in `apps/platform/shared/contracts/process-work-surface.ts:71-79,171-189`, and `apps/platform/client/features/processes/process-work-surface-page.ts:27-45,99-174` has no archive prop, no archive button, and no archive action handling.

blockingFindings.title: Derived-view rebuild can publish stale caches after archive patches
blockingFindings.evidence: `refreshViews` only compares `archiveEntryId:sequence:recordedAt` before/after rebuild (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:126-159,262-270`), but `patchArchiveEntry` can change `relatedArtifactVersionId`, `relatedSourceProvenanceId`, `relatedToolCallId`, `entryStatus`, and `degradationReason` without changing any of those fingerprint fields (`convex/archiveEntries.ts:182-226`). Those mutable fields feed turn grouping and degradation (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:210-270`). On top of that, the cold-cache GET path rebuilds and stores derived views via `warmViewsCacheOnMiss` with no conflict guard (`derived-archive-view.service.ts:53-108,173-188`). A concurrent patch can therefore repopulate turns/views from stale archive state instead of raising `ARCHIVE_DERIVATION_CONFLICT`.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Default runtime still does not emit low-level canonical archive entries
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Production boot wires the default `ScriptExecutionService` (`apps/platform/server/app.ts:285-286`), `executeFor` uses the integrated default payload (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:342-367`), and that payload hardcodes `archiveEntries: []` plus a single finalized `process_event` history item (`.../script-execution.service.ts:240-253`). The archive infrastructure accepts the full taxonomy, but the shipped default runtime only exercises compatibility-bridged history events and accepted user responses.

unresolvedItems: Whether Epic 7 intentionally stops at infrastructure-only support for low-level archive kinds in the default runtime is not stated clearly; if that is intentional, the epic/coverage docs should say so explicitly.
The stale-cache finding is code-path-derived rather than reproduced under a deterministic race test; adding a concurrency-focused regression test would help lock the behavior down.

crossStoryFindings: ArchiveFinalizationService.appendFinalizedEntry enforces non-null sourceObjectId for all entry kinds, stricter than the data contract (which marks it optional). All current callers (process-environment.service.ts, process-response.service.ts) supply non-null values, so no runtime breakage is present, but future callers that omit sourceObjectId will hit a throw rather than a graceful null.

Cache invalidation is uniformly correct across all three store implementations: archiveEntries appends invalidate archiveTurns and derivedArchiveViews; archiveTurns upserts invalidate derivedArchiveViews. This cross-story invariant is consistent in Convex, InMemoryPlatformStore, and the service layer.

ProcessHistoryCompatService maps only user_message, process_message, and process_event history kinds; progress_update, attention_request, and side_work_update are silently excluded (return null) and will never produce canonical archive entries. This is consistent with Assumption A7 and the compat bridge design.

derivedArchiveViews Convex layer uses an offset-based cursor (integer position in result set) while archiveEntries and archiveTurns use sequence/turnIndex-based cursors. Both patterns are internally consistent within their respective modules, but the asymmetry is observable at the API boundary.
architectureFindings: Production route is clean: ConvexPlatformStore delegates all archive operations to real Convex mutations and queries via makeFunctionReference. No fake adapters, stubs, or fallback logic exists in the production (ConvexPlatformStore) path.

NullPlatformStore archive methods follow the null-object pattern (hardcoded sequence:0 on appendArchiveEntry, empty pages on list methods, no-ops on upsert/replace). NullPlatformStore is never wired into production; it is used only in non-configured test/fallback scenarios.

Archive services are properly wired in app.ts: DefaultArchiveReadService, DefaultTurnDerivationService, DefaultDerivedArchiveViewService are constructed with real platformStore, processAccessService, and sourceProvenanceService dependencies, decorated onto the Fastify instance, and consumed by registered archive routes.

derivedArchiveViews Convex service-facing mutations/queries (replaceDerivedArchiveViewsForService, listDerivedArchiveViewsForService) gate access via assertValidApiKey, adding a second access-control layer beyond Fastify auth. The internal variants are internalMutation/internalQuery and not directly callable from outside Convex.

Fastify owns the finalization policy boundary (ArchiveFinalizationService) as specified; Convex owns the atomic sequence assignment and idempotency guard (by_processId_and_finalizationKey index). The separation of concerns matches the tech design decision table.
epicCoverageAssessment: AC-1.x: Full coverage. Convex appendArchiveEntry validates all seven entryKind literals, assigns sequence atomically, enforces idempotency via finalizationKey index, stores nullable related ids, and returns ArchiveEntry. Tests: TC-1.1a/b/c, TC-1.2a/b, TC-1.3a/b, TC-1.4a/b + primitive idempotency guard test.

AC-2.x: Full coverage. appendFromProcessHistoryItem gates on lifecycleState === 'finalized'; live history normalizer and process-live-normalizer remain unchanged (live/archive separation). Tests: TC-2.1a, TC-2.2a/b, TC-2.3a/b + live/archive separation test.

AC-3.x: Full coverage. Authenticated Fastify routes enforce project/process access via processAccessService.assertProcessAccess before reading; ArchiveReadService returns bounded pages with enriched entries and degraded-entry support; empty state returns valid empty page. Tests: TC-3.1a/b, TC-3.2a/b, TC-3.3a/b, TC-3.4a.

AC-4.x: Full coverage. deriveTurnsFromArchiveEntries implements all grouping rules: user_message starts a new turn, tool_result correlates via relatedToolCallId, pre-first-user-message entries form turn 0. Turns are cached as archiveTurns and rebuildable. Tests: TC-4.1a/b, TC-4.2a, TC-4.3a, TC-4.4a + turn-zero and rebuild stability tests.

AC-5.x: Full coverage. DerivedArchiveViewService generates turn_range views (one per turn) and chunk_candidate views (one per two turns) from cached turns. Views contain no model-generated summaries; bodyText is a deterministic structural label. Tests: TC-5.1a, TC-5.2a, TC-5.3a/b, TC-5.4a, TC-5.5a/b + no-summary-body enforcement test.

AC-6.x: Full coverage. enrichArchiveEntries loads artifact versions and producing-process display labels in parallel, loads source provenance entries, and propagates per-entry degradation reasons when related records are unavailable. Tests: TC-6.1a, TC-6.2a, TC-6.3a/b.

AC-7.x: Full coverage. Archive entries, turns, and views are durable (Convex) or rebuildable from archive entries. Services use warm-start cache patterns: empty cache + existing archive entries triggers rebuild on first read. Cursor pagination enforced at all three layers with configurable limits. Tests: TC-7.1a/b, TC-7.2a, TC-7.3a.
productionPathFindings: ConvexPlatformStore.appendArchiveEntry delegates to real Convex appendArchiveEntryMutation with skipQueue:true. No placeholder, no conditional bypass.

ConvexPlatformStore.replaceDerivedArchiveViews passes apiKey (from ConvexPlatformStore.apiKey) to replaceDerivedArchiveViewsForService, which internally calls assertValidApiKey before the real internalMutation. Real execution path.

NullPlatformStore.appendArchiveEntry returns a synthetic ArchiveEntry with archiveEntryId ${processId}:archive:0 and sequence:0 without writing to any store. This is the null-object pattern used in fallback/test-only contexts, not a production path. No production code path passes NullPlatformStore to archive services.
NullPlatformStore.listArchiveEntries, listArchiveTurns, and listDerivedArchiveViews return empty pages without reading any store. Same null-object pattern; same non-production scope.

The ArchiveFinalizationService integration in process-environment.service.ts (applyExecutionResultSideEffects) and process-response.service.ts (archiveAcceptedUserResponse) are real awaited calls, not fire-and-forget or silent no-ops. Failures surface to callers.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Missing convex/archiveTurns.test.ts and convex/derivedArchiveViews.test.ts
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Test plan specifies separate Convex test files for turn upsert/list and derived-view replace/list primitives. Neither file exists. Coverage for these mutations is present in convex/archiveEntries.test.ts integration tests (which test turn derivation and view creation end-to-end), but isolated primitive tests for archiveTurns.ts and derivedArchiveViews.ts are absent.

nonBlockingFindings.title: ArchiveFinalizationService.appendFinalizedEntry requires non-null sourceObjectId for all entry kinds
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: archive-finalization.service.ts line 31-33: if (sourceObjectId === null) { throw new Error('Finalized ${args.entryKind} entries require a sourceObjectId.'); }. The data contract (epic.md, tech-design.md) marks sourceObjectId as optional. All current callers supply non-null values, but the mismatch means any future caller that legitimately omits sourceObjectId will receive a runtime throw rather than a clean null path.

nonBlockingFindings.title: findExistingEntryBySourceObjectId performs full paginated archive scan
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: archive-finalization.service.ts lines 106-133: appendFromProcessHistoryItem checks for a duplicate user_message entry by scanning all archive pages in a do-while loop (limit 200 per page). This is O(n) on archive size. For processes with thousands of archive entries, this can add significant latency to user_message finalization. No index on (processId, sourceObjectId) exists in the Convex schema.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived views use offset-based cursor pagination inconsistent with archive entry and turn cursors
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: convex/derivedArchiveViews.ts listDerivedArchiveViews: cursor is decoded as integer offset (decodedCursor); query fetches limit + decodedCursor + 1 rows and slices from offset. In contrast, archiveEntries and archiveTurns use sequence/turnIndex GT comparisons for stable cursor semantics. If derived views are replaced between page fetches, offset-based pagination can skip or repeat items.

nonBlockingFindings.title: MAX_DERIVED_ARCHIVE_VIEW_LIMIT equals DEFAULT_DERIVED_ARCHIVE_VIEW_LIMIT (50); long processes approach page limit
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: derived-archive-view.service.ts lines 22-23: DEFAULT_DERIVED_ARCHIVE_VIEW_LIMIT = 50, MAX_DERIVED_ARCHIVE_VIEW_LIMIT = 50. DerivedArchiveViewService generates one turn_range view per turn and one chunk_candidate per two turns. A process with 34 turns produces 34 + 17 = 51 derived views, exceeding the 50-item page limit. The first page truncates results without a next-page path being surfaced to the client sections.
